claims.question: Does region 0x006B1C60-0x006B1E00 contain a concrete factory/resource->actualS identity bridge (registration key, receiver pointer, elem+8 store)?
claims.statement: The admitted window contains NO concrete factory/resource->actualS identity bridge. Complete store census of all 126 rows: the only non-frame stores are [EAX]=0xa85454 (vtable install, 006b1c62), [0x00BA7220]=0x1 (flag, 006b1c68), [EDI]=EAX (deque insert into local container storage, 006b1d0a) and container-field saves. There is NO store to any [elem+8], no receiver-pointer store, no resource-ID/key comparison, and no keyed lookup anywhere in the window. The only +8 accesses are vtable-slot READS ([EAX+8] @006b1d89, [EDX+8] @006b1da4) feeding virtual calls.
premises: Window is end-exclusive at 0x006B1E00; body 006B1C80 continues beyond the window (in-window JZ targets 006b1f28/006b1f34 prove body extent).
GA3 premise (postaudit): vtable 00A85454 = ArkModelResourceItemFactory class; vtable install is class identity, not receiver identity.
vtable match != runtime receiver identity (preserved distinction).
claims.countermodel: The bridge (a keyed registration, [elem+8]=receiver store, or resource-ID lookup) could exist in the un-admitted tail of 006B1C80 (0x006B1E00 onward, incl. 006b1e2f leaf path and 006b1f28/006b1f34 exits), in the caller of 006B1C60, or in W1/cache code. This package cannot exclude those locations; the absence claim is scoped to the window.

claims.question: What IS in the region 0x006B1C60-0x006B1E00?
claims.statement: The region contains: (a) a 4-row vtable-install/flag stub 006B1C60 (installs factory class vtable 00A85454 into [ECX], sets global flag [0xBA7220]=1) — a class-bootstrap, not resource registration; (b) a worklist-based type-directed scene-graph walker 006B1C80 (partial in window) that seeds one stack argument (a root pointer, by value) into a locally-constructed deque, pops elements, calls elem->vtable+8 (typeinfo-style virtual), walks [result+4] parent chains, matches static type node 0xBA7218 to take the branch path (children iterated via [elem+0xCC] data pointer and [elem+0xD4] count, 4-byte stride) and pushes each child back into the worklist; matches node 0xBA7210 to take a leaf path at 006b1e2f (beyond window); frees its own 0x80-byte deque chunks via indirect [0x00A759FC](chunk,0x80) as it advances.
premises: NiTArray layout premise (+C8 object, +CC data pointer, +D4 count) — independently cross-confirmed here on branch elements (see P01-C7).
Deque/worklist implementation inference (0x80-byte chunks, map pointer, insert cursor, capacity) is pattern-based from explicit dataflow; std-library naming is NOT asserted.

The walker's single stack argument (ARG1=[ESP+0x70]) is passed by value; which pointer the caller (006B1FD0 context) passes is outside the window — postaudit premise places 006B1C80 between V_first @006B201A and arg reload @006B206C.
claims.countermodel: 006B1C80 could be a non-scene traversal (any graph walk with type-tagged nodes); the 'scene-graph' reading follows from the +CC/+D4 children layout matching the known NiTArray children premise and from postaudit context that this body sits on the model-load path. The traversal mechanics themselves are explicit in-window dataflow.
claims.evidence_level: CONFIRMED (mechanics scoped to window; 'scene-graph walker' naming STRONGLY_SUPPORTED)

claims.question: Does type66+ID A suffice to join 296445?
claims.statement: The admitted windows provide NO evidence that type66+ID A suffices to join 296445: no (type,id)-keyed logic exists in either window (no 66/0x42 immediate, no ID comparisons, no keyed table access). Identity logic in region 1 is exclusively vtable-dispatch + static type-node chain matching (0xBA7218/0xBA7210), which carries no resource ID. The (type,id)->resource->receiver join mechanism remains unaddressed by this package.

evidence.method: immediate-value and comparison census over all 236 in-window rows; only integer immediates present are container sizes (0x4c,0x4,0x80,0x8,0x1,0x6,0x5,0x0), RTTI node addresses (0xba7210,0xba7218), vtable addresses (0xa85454,0xa8ec24,0xa8ea78,0xa8e9e8), SEH constants (0xa02761,0xa1fbdf,0x00b9d8d0), allocator tokens (0x79fc70,0x00a759fc). No 66 (0x42) and no resource-ID-like compares.

premises: Preserved distinction: identical lookup shapes / vtable matches do not prove common semantics.

Front C context (parent contract): type66 and ID A are definition-side identifiers; their join to resource 296445 requires a keyed registry/lookup channel that this package did not find in its windows.
claims.countermodel: A (type,id)-keyed join could exist elsewhere (definition/registry code, W1 cache, resource table); nothing in this package rules it in or out — the windows simply contain no such logic.
claims.evidence_level: CONFIRMED (absence of keyed logic in windows)
claims.claim_resolution: NOT_ESTABLISHED (global join question unchanged; no new supporting evidence)

claims.question: Scoped write-set/alias analysis of 006B1C80: can it write the outslot or V, changing Q preservation premises?
claims.statement: Within the admitted window, 006B1C80's explicit stores are frame-local or local-deque-internal only. The previously-open store [EDI]=EAX (006b1d0a) is now pinned: EDI = [ESP+0x2c], the insert-cursor field of the locally-constructed deque whose 10-dword header is zero-initialized in-frame (006b1cbe-006b1ce2) and managed by 0043ba10/0043ca60; EAX = ARG1 = [ESP+0x70] = the single by-value stack argument. The store therefore writes the caller-supplied root value into the walker's own worklist storage, not into the caller's frame. No explicit store in the window reaches the caller's outslot or V cell, and the body receives no pointer to either (only ARG1 by value).

evidence.frame_arithmetic: prologue consumes 0x6C below entry ESP => [ESP+0x70] = first stack arg = [entryESP+4]; PUSH EBP at 006b1cb4 is the 0-argument to CALL 0043ba10 (callee-popped), not a this-save.

premises: Postaudit open point being resolved: 'EDI comes from a local container; without EDI origin no guarantee of not affecting another slot' — origin now pinned to the local deque cursor field.

Heap/stack disjointness remains a PREMISE, not runtime fact: if 0043ba10/0043ca60 could return chunk storage overlapping the caller's live frame, the [EDI]=EAX store could hit a caller slot; this is excluded only by the allocator premise.
Explicit CFG store != final memory value after opaque calls (preserved).
claims.countermodel: Residual opaque channels that could still write outslot/V (none syntactically argument-reachable, all premise-level): (a) 0043ba10/0043ca60 allocator aliasing (see premise above); (b) the two virtual elem->vtable+8 calls (006b1d8e CALL EDX, 006b1da9 CALL EAX) receive ECX=elem only, where elements derive from caller-supplied ARG1 — a member-internal alias (e.g., a global holding a stack address) remains unexcluded at premise level; (c) indirect [0x00A759FC] free of the deque's own chunks.
claims.claim_resolution: REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE for explicit-store write of outslot/V (scoped to window); premise-level countermodels preserved and enumerated

claims.question: What is callee 007D27B0 (admitted region 0x007D27B0-0x007D291E), called after *out stores in 0082E750?
claims.statement: 007D27B0 is a NiStream teardown/destructor-class body, complete in window (110 rows, plain RET): installs vptr 0x00A8EC24 at [this] on entry (007d27d9 — same vptr the postaudit observed on the NiStream in 0082E750); releases members at +0x15C/+0x160/+0x128 via virtual slot0 calls with argument 1 (release pattern); refcount-decrements and conditionally destroys the member at +0x194 (twice, second pass also nulls the field); calls internal 007d1d70(this) and 007d16b0(this+0x184); frees owned buffers at +0x174, +0x164, +0x148, +0x130, +0x8 via 0095db40 (with [ptr-4] prefix reads and 0095dd6c(0x79fc70,[ptr-4],4,ptr) calls for +148/+130); resets sub-vptr fields [this+0x144]=0xA8EA78, [this+0x12C]=0xA8EA78, [this+0x4]=0xA8E9E8.
premises: Postaudit premise: NiStream object in 0082E750 carries vptr 00A8EC24 and is a local on the producer's stack (explains plain RET without self-free).

Dtor-class interpretation rests on: redundant derived-vptr install at entry + base sub-vptr resets + free-all-members pattern. Whether it is the final dtor or a Close()/Shutdown() on an object about to die does not change the write-set conclusion.
claims.countermodel: It could be a reset/reuse function rather than a final dtor; either way the body leaves the object with all owned buffers freed and sub-vptrs reset, and the write-set analysis (P01-C6) is unaffected.
claims.evidence_level: CONFIRMED (body mechanics scoped to window; dtor-class naming STRONGLY_SUPPORTED)
claims.claim_resolution: CONDITIONAL (dtor vs Close naming); mechanics CONFIRMED

claims.question: Can 007D27B0 write the outslot or V (alias/argument), changing Q preservation premises?
claims.statement: No explicit store or argument of 007D27B0 can reach the 0082E750 outslot or V cell: its only argument is ECX=this (no stack args; PUSH ECX at entry is a slot allocation); its complete explicit write set is this-relative ([this], [this+4], [this+12C], [this+144], [this+194], [member+4] refcount decrements) plus frame/SEH. No pointer to the outslot or V cell is passed in. Therefore the explicit-store channel from 0082E750's post-store opaque call 007D27B0 to outslot/V is closed (scoped: explicit stores).

evidence.source_lines: 995327-995436 (complete store census; all MOV-to-memory targets enumerated in ANALYSIS_NOTES R3)

premises: Heap/stack disjointness and live-local disjointness are PREMISES: the countermodel 'outslot or V cell lies inside [this..this+0x194] of the destructed NiStream' is excluded only by the assumption that distinct live locals do not overlap in the producer's frame.
Explicit CFG store != final memory value after opaque calls (preserved).
claims.countermodel: Premise-level residual channels (unproven negatives, preserved): (a) outslot/V cell inside the NiStream's own field range (excluded by frame-layout premise only); (b) member virtual releases (+15C/+160/+128/+194), internal 007d1d70/007d16b0, or free-family 0095db40/0095dd6c writing through member-internal or allocator-internal aliases — no syntactic channel passes a caller-frame pointer to any of them.
claims.claim_resolution: REJECTED_WITH_EVIDENCE for explicit-store/argument write of outslot/V; premise-level countermodels preserved

claims.question: Does 007D27B0 change Q preservation premises in any other way?
claims.statement: YES — a lifetime premise refinement: 007D27B0 FREES the [this+0x148] holder buffer (007d288a MOV EAX,[ESI+0x148]; TEST; free path 007d28a6-007d28c0). Per the postaudit dataflow premise, +0x148 is the exact holder dereferenced in the post-load read V=M32[M32[obj+0x148]]. After 007D27B0 runs, the V-holder is dangling. Therefore: (1) any later re-read of the holder would be use-after-free/dangling — invalid; (2) survival of the V value (and hence *out/Q) after 0082E750 depends on the retain (refcount) performed in 0082E750 ('store *out=V and retain' premise), NOT on holder liveness. Q0/Q1/VT preservation arguments must not assume the +0x148 holder outlives the NiStream teardown.

evidence.cited_premise: PE_935_CAND4_Q_DEEP_POSTAUDIT_R1_20261018/REPORT.md: 'Po sukcesie AL następuje odczyt V=M32[M32[obj+148h]], przetwarzanie V, store *out=V i retain.'

premises: The +0x148 field identity between this body's `this` and the V-read `obj` rests on both carrying the NiStream vptr 00A8EC24 (postaudit premise; same class).
Whether the retain fully protects V on ALL paths of 0082E750 is outside both windows — not claimable here.
claims.countermodel: If some path stores *out without the retain, V's object could be released by later refcount drops (including possibly inside member teardown) — this package cannot rule that out; it only pins that the HOLDER itself is freed here.
claims.evidence_level: STRONGLY_SUPPORTED (the +0x148 free is CONFIRMED in-window; its bearing on V/Q uses the cited postaudit dataflow premise)
claims.claim_resolution: CONDITIONAL refinement of Q-preservation premises: holder-liveness premise must be dropped; retain-dependence premise must be tracked
